mechanism_claims.claim_text: RP556 and R10 were tested in LPS-stimulated human PBMNC cultures; RP556 increased IL-10 and had a smaller TNF-alpha increase, while R10 reduced TNF-alpha/IL-10 responses in the reported conditions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is cytokine modulation in human PBMNC culture, not an in vivo wound-healing or antibacterial killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: FITC-labeled RP556 localized at the E. coli cell membrane, and R10 was reported to behave similarly in the confocal microscopy experiment.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The authors note that FITC labeling could alter physicochemical properties, so this supports membrane localization rather than a fully resolved killing model.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Langmuir-Blodgett monolayer experiments showed RP556 and R10 intercalated into the Gram-negative model membrane and slightly reduced collapse pressure.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The monolayer model is a membrane model system; it should not be over-promoted to a complete intact-cell mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper reports MIC-based antibacterial phenotype across ESKAPE-related bacteria and C. acnes, but does not identify a single intracellular molecular target.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: all tested peptides; strongest broad-spectrum emphasis on RP556 and R10
mechanism_claims.limitations: Preserve as phenotype/context evidence; do not convert MIC tables into a direct molecular target claim.
